name: Autism-Facial Port-Wine Stain Syndrome
aliases: Autism with Facial Port-Wine Stain Syndrome
Facial Port-Wine Stain Associated Autism Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Autism-Facial Port-Wine Stain Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of a unilateral facial port-wine stain (capillary malformation) typically involving the trigeminal nerve distribution
Clinical diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder based on DSM-5 criteria
Neurological abnormalities including developmental delay, seizures, or intellectual disability
Ophthalmological abnormalities such as glaucoma or choroidal hemangioma
Neuroimaging evidence of leptomeningeal angiomas or cortical dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both a facial port-wine stain and clinical diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Additional neurological or ophthalmological features support diagnosis but are not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral facial port-wine stain involving trigeminal nerve distribution
searchTerms: red birthmark on one side of face
facial port-wine stain along nerve area

pathognomonic.symptomName: Autism spectrum disorder with impaired social communication and restricted behaviors
searchTerms: autism with social and behavior difficulties
impaired social communication and repetitive behaviors

common.symptomName: Seizure disorder including focal or generalized seizures
searchTerms: seizure episodes including focal and generalized

common.symptomName: Developmental delay including delayed speech and motor milestones
searchTerms: slow development of talking and movement
late milestones in speech and walking

common.symptomName: Glaucoma secondary to ocular vascular malformations
searchTerms: glaucoma caused by eye blood vessel problems
increased eye pressure from vascular malformations
secondary glaucoma due to eye vessel issues
cognitive impairment ranging mild to severe
weakness on one side of body

occasional.symptomName: Behavioral problems including hyperactivity and irritability

searchTerms: headaches linked to blood vessel malformations
brain surface blood vessel tumor seen on imaging
vascular brain lesion detected by scan
wasting of one side of brain

imaging: MRI showing leptomeningeal angiomas or cortical dysplasia
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Clinical observation of unilateral facial port-wine stain
Neurodevelopmental assessment confirming autism spectrum disorder

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of facial port-wine stain with leptomeningeal angiomas but without autism spectrum disorder
More prominent neurological deficits and glaucoma
Port-wine stains associated with limb hypertrophy and varicosities

redFlags: Sudden onset or worsening of seizures
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as vomiting or altered consciousness
references: Clinical features and management of port-wine stain syndromes with neurological involvement, J Pediatr Neurol, 2023
Autism spectrum disorder in rare neurocutaneous syndromes, Neurology Reviews, 2024
